$comment: Per-repo config for the org source-leak-gate caller (.github/workflows/source-leak-gate.yml). This repo carries a local copy of the actions-pinned-gate engine (scripts/audit/actions-pinned-gate.mjs + its test), whose source and tests necessarily contain the version-comment markers they enforce (`# vX.Y.Z` after a pinned SHA) — exactly like the source-leak scanner's own rule definitions contain the markers it detects. The skills-drift-gate.yml caller (cinatra#188) carries the literal gate name `skills-drift-gate`, which the source-leak SLG_PLANNING_DOC rule treats as a `drift-gate` planning-artifact marker — a self-referential false positive identical in kind to the actions-pinned-gate case, mirroring the exemption cinatra-ai/ci applies to its own copy in config/self-check.json. The dashboards v1.2 migration `core__0006_dashboards-v12.mjs` (cinatra#327) is inherently a marker-bearing artifact: it migrates legacy dashboard rows TO the dashboard config schema's literal `apiVersion` value `v1.2` (the existing DASHBOARD_CONFIG_V12_VERSION constant), so its SQL literals (`config_version = 'v1.2'`) and prose unavoidably carry the bare `vN.N` token the SLG_MILESTONE_VERSION rule matches — NOT a release-milestone reference. That is the same self-referential class as the gate-engine exemptions; the shared schema files (drizzle-store.ts/store/schema.ts) that also gain a single `v1.2` default are deliberately NOT exempted (they carry an inline uppercase _VERSION marker so only that line is excused). The `branch-protections.json` documentation-of-record manifest lists the live `required_status_checks.contexts`, which legitimately include the literal required-check name `skills-drift-gate / skills-drift-gate`; the source-leak SLG_PLANNING_DOC rule treats that embedded `drift-gate` substring as a planning-artifact marker — a self-referential false positive identical in kind to the skills-drift-gate.yml caller exemption already present (the file must carry the real gate name to document live protection). The release-governance drift gates add the same self-referential class: the `governance-drift-gate.yml` caller carries the literal gate name `governance-drift-gate`, and its companion `governance-drift-allowlist.json` plus the `secrets-required.txt` manifest entry for the gate's token reference that name in prose — the SLG_PLANNING_DOC rule reads the `drift-gate` substring as a planning-artifact marker, an unavoidable false positive identical in kind to the `skills-drift-gate.yml` caller and `branch-protections.json` cases (the files must carry the real gate name to wire/document it). The cinatra#979 extension-conformance-gate ships a PRIVATE-org-repo-reference DENYLIST (`PRIVATE_ORG_REPO_SLUGS` in scripts/extensions/lib/conformance-rules.mjs) that a public extension repo's own hygiene check is run against — the same self-referential class as every exemption above: the file whose JOB is to detect a marker must contain that marker as data. Its test fixtures (scripts/extensions/__tests__/conformance-gate.test.mjs) exercise both the positive case (a private-repo mention IS flagged) and the negative case (a public shared-tooling repo, e.g. `cinatra-ai/extension-release-tooling`, is NOT), so the test file legitimately carries both name classes too; the reusable workflow (.github/workflows/extension-conformance-gate-reusable.yml) documents its relationship to that same public tooling repo in a comment. Those three files are exempted by basename. The engineering#484 merge-group coverage guard (`scripts/ci/merge-group-coverage-guard.mjs` + its test) is the same self-referential class once more: its REQUIRED_CONTEXTS mirror of the live branch-protection required checks must carry the literal context name `skills-drift-gate / skills-drift-gate` as DATA (and the test asserts that very string), so the SLG_PLANNING_DOC `drift-gate` substring unavoidably appears — identical in kind to the `branch-protections.json` documentation-of-record exemption. The cinatra#2986 dev-lock auto-bump recipe adds the same self-referential class once more: the rolling bump PR must itself satisfy `skills-drift-gate`, so the workflow that opens it (`.github/workflows/dev-lock-auto-bump.yml`), the body composer that PRESERVES a human acknowledgement for that gate (`scripts/ci/dev-lock-bump-pr-body.mjs`), and the derivation that reads the gate caller's own pins (`scripts/ci/skills-drift-watched-packages.mjs`, whose GATE_CALLER constant IS that caller's path) each carry the literal gate name to wire and document that relationship — the SLG_PLANNING_DOC rule reads the embedded `drift-gate` substring as a planning-artifact marker, identical in kind to the `skills-drift-gate.yml` caller and `merge-group-coverage-guard.mjs` exemptions above. Their two test files are deliberately NOT exempted: they import the path constant instead of the literal, so they stay under the scanner. The product-tree hygiene gate (owner ruling 2026-08-28) refuses development-artifact directories in the tracked tree, `.planning/` among them. ONLY its test (`scripts/ci/__tests__/product-tree-hygiene.test.mjs`) is exempted, and only because a gate's negative cases cannot be written without the very strings the gate detects: the fixture rows `.planning/ROADMAP.md` and `packages/x/.planning/PLAN.md` MUST contain that path for the rule under test to fire at all, which SLG_PLANNING_PATH reads as an internal planning directory and SLG_PLANNING_DOC reads as planning-artifact filenames. They are synthetic string literals in an assertion table — no such file exists in this repo, which is precisely what the gate they test guarantees. The ENGINE (`scripts/ci/product-tree-hygiene.mjs`) is deliberately NOT exempted: it holds the forbidden names as bare directory tokens without a trailing slash, which no rule matches, so it stays fully under the scanner. Narrower than the `actions-pinned-gate.mjs` and `merge-group-coverage-guard.mjs` engine+test pairs above, which exempt both halves. Nothing else is exempted.
$comment_lineExcludes: OAS-RUNTIME-<NNN> are PUBLIC deterministic OAS runtime-invariant lint codes emitted by packages/agents/src/validate-oas-runtime-invariants.ts and documented in docs/developing-agents.md (the human-readable per-code guidance) — a stable, greppable public code series, NOT an internal requirement/workstream tracker ID. The SLG_REQ_ID_BROAD heuristic (multi-segment PREFIX-SEG-NNN shape, no contextExclude) cannot distinguish them and grandfathered the pre-existing OAS-RUNTIME-001..008 via the line ratchet; net-new codes in the same series (the #924 artifact-parity family 009..012) would otherwise trip it on every addition. This line-scoped exclude covers only lines carrying an `OAS-RUNTIME-<3 digits>` token (present and future codes, in the rule engine, its tests, and the scan-all wiring) — the deliberately-public path the engine documents for exactly this false-positive class. The cinatra#2591 knowledge-graph embedder floor adds a second deliberately-public token of the same class: `bge-small-en-v1.5` is the upstream HuggingFace identifier of the sentence-transformers model baked into docker/kg-embedder — a third-party MODEL NAME whose trailing `v1.5` the SLG_MILESTONE_VERSION heuristic reads as a cinatra release-milestone reference. It is not one: it names an external artifact, it must be spelled exactly to resolve, and it necessarily appears wherever the model is pinned (the build ARG, the server default, the compose/config defaults, and the works-after arm that must run the SAME model for its dimensions to match). This line-scoped exclude covers only lines carrying that model token, so every other `vN.N` on those files stays under the scanner.
